s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
key_facts: 1 day of chest pressure
Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
Substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Diaphoresis
1 episode of vomiting
Vital signs within normal limits
Normal cardiac examination
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level: 6.18 ng/mL
ECG findings: ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
Normal left ventricular end-diastolic pressure
Normal transthoracic echocardiogram results

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, ECG changes, and chest pain with radiation to the jaw

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression and chest pain

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, normal coronary arteries, and chest pain

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and chest pain with radiation to the jaw, although coronary angiography was normal

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with radiation to the jaw, diaphoresis, and elevated troponin

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated troponin, and ECG changes, along with the recent history of subjective fevers and normal coronary arteries, suggests an inflammatory process affecting both the myocardium and pericardium.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries and lack of evidence for coronary artery disease

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Elevated troponin and ECG changes suggest myocardial involvement, not just pericardial

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: ECG findings and elevated inflammatory markers suggest pericardial involvement in addition to myocardial
